annotations.description: Casting Ocelot Pride in the precombat main phase rather than Voice of Victory is debatable. Voice of Victory (1W) would tap out but provides Mobilize 2 (creating two attacking tokens when it attacks) AND prevents the opponent from casting spells during your turn. With Urza's Saga at 2 lore counters, the opponent will get chapter III next turn to search for an artifact. Voice of Victory's 'opponents can't cast spells during your turn' doesn't stop that, but Voice's board presence with Mobilize is significant. However, Ocelot Pride with Guide of Souls does generate value through life gain triggers and end-step token creation. The real question is whether casting a creature before combat (when holding Thraben Charm as a trick) matters - Guide of Souls could attack first, and then casting Ocelot Pride post-combat would still trigger Guide's ETB for life/energy, and Ocelot Pride would still see the life gain for end-step triggers. Playing Ocelot Pride pre-combat gives the opponent information before attacks.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Ocelot Pride (W) precombat, leaving W open
annotations.betterLine: Attack with Guide of Souls first, then cast Ocelot Pride post-combat (Guide of Souls ETB trigger still gives life gain for Ocelot Pride's end step trigger, and you don't reveal information before attacks)

annotations.description: Casting Ragavan without Dash in post-combat main means it can't attack this turn and won't generate value until next turn. The opponent has Urza's Saga at 2 lore counters and will search for an artifact next turn (chapter III), plus they have access to mana for removal. Ragavan is vulnerable to being removed before it ever attacks. However, if it survives, having it permanently on the battlefield is better than Dashing it, and casting it post-combat is fine since there's no way to attack with it this turn regardless. The main concern is that Dash would have been safer against potential removal, bouncing back to hand if the opponent has answers, but the upside of a permanent Ragavan that triggers Guide of Souls every turn is significant. Additionally, Guide of Souls triggers on Ragavan entering, gaining 1 life and 1 energy, which is valuable. This is a reasonable decision overall.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Ragavan with normal cost {R} to keep it on the battlefield permanently
annotations.betterLine: Dash might have been slightly safer given the opponent could have removal, but normal cast is defensible since Ragavan staying on board is higher upside and triggers Guide of Souls for life/energy

annotations.description: Casting Galvanic Discharge on Emry pre-combat is reasonable since Emry enables recurring artifacts from the graveyard (including Lavaspur Boots, Mox Opals, etc.), but doing it before combat means losing the option to use Galvanic Discharge as a combat trick or holding it for a potentially bigger threat. However, with Voice of Victory preventing the opponent from casting spells during your turn, and having 6 creatures to attack with, the player could consider whether attacking first with the full board (potentially getting lethal or near-lethal damage through) before spending mana on removal would be better. With Guide of Souls (1/2), Ocelot Pride (1/1), Cat Token (1/1), Ragavan (2/1), and Voice of Victory (1/3) plus potential Mobilize tokens, that's significant damage. Removing Emry is reasonable though since it's a major value engine that can recur artifacts every turn.

annotations.betterLine: Attack first with all creatures (Voice of Victory creates Mobilize tokens and prevents opponent from casting spells during your turn anyway), then evaluate whether to use Galvanic Discharge post-combat. Emry is summoning sick and can't activate this turn, so there's no urgency to remove it before your combat phase.
